thread:
maria: picking up an escalation from Acme — they hit a traffic spike and started getting intermittent 429s and p95 spikes even though they have Dedicated capacity :confused:

maria: stack traces/logs show repeated 'burst_window_exceeded' and 'rate_limited' responses for some routes, but other routes look fine. attaching short excerpts below.

infra-bot: alert: route=acme-chat-prod burst_window_exceeded count=183 windowsize_ms=60000

maria: repro steps they gave: many short requests (~30-120 tokens) across many distinct conversation ids (different prefixes). they said per-minute token usage is under commit, but requests spike in brief bursts.

support: can you paste a minimal repro we can run locally? also need the route config (batching/kvcache) and any SDK usage pattern.

maria: here's the curl loop they used (simplified):

```
for i in $(seq 1 500); do 
  curl -s -X POST "https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate" \
    -H "Authorization: Bearer $KEY" \
    -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
    -d '{"model":"open-rl-7b","prompt":"hi #'$i'","max_tokens":40}' &
done
wait
```

maria: they also have a little more realistic client that sets conversation_id to a UUID per short chat turn, so high prefix diversity -> many distinct KV keys.

anya: this smells like continuous batching + kvcache prefetch thrash. if each request touches a unique prefix, batch sizes collapse and kv-prefetch floods the runtime, causing backpressure that surfaces as perceived throttling/429s.

anya: can you share route config? specifically: batching.max_batch_tokens, batching.max_wait_ms, kvcache.prefetch (true/false), and route.burst_window?

maria: route snippet they sent (redacted):

```
route: acme-chat-prod
  batching:
    max_batch_tokens: 2048
    max_wait_ms: 50
  kvcache:
    prefetch: true
    max_prefetch_keys: 32
  burst:
    window_ms: 60000
    max_requests: 100
```

sam: thanks. hypotheses: 1) prefetch==true + many unique prefixes -> lots of small warmups and kv misses; 2) small max_wait_ms causes many tiny batches; 3) burst.max_requests configured lower than transient fanout. combined effect -> runtime tripping burst window and returning 429s.

sam: quick repro I ran locally: spawn 200 concurrent short requests with random prefix -> median batch occupancy drops to 1-2 and kv hit rate ~5%. runtime queue length spikes and we see internal 429s.

maria: customer tried a quick mitigation: set kvcache.prefetch=false and bumped burst.max_requests -> 429s dropped immediately, p95 improved. CPU went up about 15% which they expected.

support: good short-term fix. for a long term, we should recommend either: increase route burst_window / max_requests, or reduce batch max_wait_ms to allow slightly larger batches? caution: reducing max_wait_ms makes batches smaller, so actually increase max_wait_ms to encourage aggregation.

anya: right — increasing batching.max_wait_ms (to e.g., 100-200ms) usually increases occupancy for many small requests and amortizes KV lookups. alternative: enable prefix grouping on the client (same conversation_id per session) or shard hot keys so prefetch is effective.

sam: actionable items for support/SRE:
- collect runtime metrics around batch_size distribution, kvcache.hits/misses, and queue length from last 30m (use /internal/metrics endpoint).
- ask customer to run a controlled test: same QPS but group requests into 10 logical prefixes to see improvement.
- propose a config change: set kvcache.prefetch=false temporarily, increase burst.max_requests to 300, and set batching.max_wait_ms=150, then monitor.

support: commands to get metrics:
```
curl -s -H "Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN_KEY" "https://controlplane.redwood.internal/debug/metrics?route=acme-chat-prod" | jq . | egrep "batch_size|kvcache|queue"
```

support: also collect a handful of trace ids for 429 responses so runtime team can correlate internal error codes.

maria: customer reports they already tried grouping prefixes and saw much lower 429s — confirms hypothesis. they want guidance to avoid raising costs too much.

anya: long-term fixes:
- tune kvcache.prefetch heuristics (avoid prefetch for extremely high prefix cardinality workloads),
- implement adaptive batching that increases max_wait when batch occupancy low,
- expose a per-route 'burst_shield' that gracefully queues instead of 429s for short windows (requires SRE change).

sam: I'll open infra ticket with the runtime owners and attach the metrics + traces. will propose a preflight playbook for customers hitting this pattern.

support: noted — please include recommended guardrails for costs (e.g., estimate CPU increase when disabling prefetch).

maria: thanks all. I'll send the customer the short mitigation steps and ask for the trace ids.

sam: tagging @anya to follow the runtime tuning discussion.

anya: on it. :thumbsup:

maria: closing loop here once infra ticket is created. thanks everyone!"
